# Three.js AAA Graphics Builder

## Purpose

Own the production graphics pass. Convert basic screenshots into authored, high-density, performance-aware visual experiences.

## Use When

Screenshots still look basic, models look primitive, worlds are sparse, UI/world art feels generic, or the user asks for premium, AAA, high-fidelity, showcase, or less-basic graphics.

## Required References

These references are required phase-entry gates, not optional reading:

- Load `references/visual-scorecard.md` before scoring, judging completion, or making any premium/AAA/showcase claim.
- Load `references/implementation-blueprint.md` before changing graphics architecture, materials, VFX, rendering, diagnostics, or broad visual systems.
- Load `references/model-recipes.md` before building or upgrading hero/player, obstacle, enemy, pickup, world-kit, material, or prop models.
- Load `references/render-recipes.md` before changing lighting, tone mapping, shadows, fog, post-processing, materials, or render composition.
- Load `references/technical-art.md` before premium/AAA/showcase graphics work, shaders/material systems, VFX systems, generated/imported asset cleanup, LOD/instancing work, or visual changes that could affect browser performance.
- Load `references/shader-cookbook.md` before writing any custom shader, `onBeforeCompile` injection, material recipe, sky, or post-processing chain — use its proven values and GLSL patterns instead of improvising.
- Load `references/checklists/aaa-game-quality-gate.md` and `references/checklists/aaa-visual-scorecard.md` before declaring a game premium, AAA, showcase, complete, release-ready, or less basic.
- Load the relevant checklist before focused work: `references/checklists/procedural-model-quality.md`, `references/checklists/material-lighting-quality.md`, `references/checklists/performance-safe-visual-detail.md`, or `references/checklists/technical-art-quality.md`.
- Load `references/prompt-templates.md` only when the user asks for reusable prompts, a graphics-pass prompt, or a task template.

For broad "still looks basic", premium, AAA, high-fidelity, showcase, or less-basic graphics work, load all five references as the first action in the phase. Track them in a reference ledger with yes/no, path, and failure reason. Do not mark the graphics phase complete while any required reference is skipped.

External asset sourcing gate:

- For premium/AAA/showcase/high-fidelity/less-basic graphics with a hero/player, character, creature, boss, vehicle, ship, building, weapon, signature prop, complex pickup, or hero environment piece, load `threejs-3d-generator` before deciding procedural geometry is enough.
- For premium/AAA/showcase/high-fidelity/less-basic graphics with concept needs, texture/material references, decals, logos, faction marks, icons, GUI art, skies, backgrounds, title/menu art, or image-to-3D inputs, load `threejs-image-generator` before deciding 2D external assets are not needed.

## Workflow

1. Capture or inspect active desktop/mobile screenshots.
2. Score visuals across art direction, hero/player, obstacles, rewards, world, materials, render, VFX, UI, and performance evidence.
3. Add missing graphics architecture: material library, procedural textures/decals, model factories, world prop kit, technical-art budget, VFX system, render pipeline, diagnostics.
4. Run the credential probe, then fill the external asset sourcing ledger per surface: procedural Three.js factory, `threejs-image-generator` 2D reference/texture, `threejs-3d-generator` 3D generation, or a hybrid.

Do not make primitives look AAA by adding glow. First build authored forms, then materials, then lighting, then effects.

1: # Visual Scorecard
2: 
3: Score active-play screenshots, not idle title screens or isolated showroom models. Use desktop and mobile screenshots when mobile is in scope.
4: 
5: Scores are self-assessed against the anchors below, so they drift optimistic. Two countermeasures are mandatory for premium/AAA/showcase claims: cite Measured Evidence for the categories it supports, and run the Fresh-Eyes Review before finalizing.
6: 
7: ## Calibration Anchors
8: 
9: Reference screenshots for score calibration are packaged in `threejs-aaa-graphics-builder/assets/scorecard-anchors/`:
10: 
11: - `scene-1.jpg` — score ~1: primitive player and pickups on a flat sparse arena, utility HUD.
12: - `scene-2.jpg` — score ~2: authored track kit, imported hero asset, designed genre HUD, intentional lighting.
13: - `scene-3.jpg` — score ~2.5-3: dense layered world in active play, readable hero silhouette, event VFX, cohesive HUD.
14: 
15: Before scoring World/environment, Hero/player, Materials/textures, or Lighting/render, view the anchors and compare: if your screenshot reads closer to `scene-1.jpg` than `scene-3.jpg` for that surface, the category is at most a 1-2 regardless of how much code was written.
16: 
17: ## Scoring Scale
18: 
19: - 0: Placeholder. Default primitives, sparse world, unreadable state, debug UI, or no evidence.
20: - 1: Basic styled. Playable and themed, but still obvious prototype assets, flat composition, repeated silhouettes, or generic UI.
21: - 2: Premium stylized. Authored silhouettes, material/detail systems, readable state, cohesive UI/world, measured performance.
22: - 3: Showcase. Strong art direction, memorable hero and world, dense authored detail, excellent readability, polished VFX/rendering, and diagnostics.
23: 
24: ## Categories
25: 
26: 1. Art direction.
27:    - 0: No clear theme.
28:    - 1: Theme is mostly colors/fog.
29:    - 2: Theme affects forms, materials, UI, world, and feedback.
30:    - 3: Distinct identity visible in every surface.
31: 2. Hero/player.
32:    - 0: Default primitive stack.
33:    - 1: Basic object with glow or simple attachments.
34:    - 2: Authored silhouette, decals/trim, state cues, collision proxy.
35:    - 3: Memorable model with layered construction and expressive feedback.
36: 3. Obstacles/enemies.
37:    - 0: Cubes/cones/spheres.
38:    - 1: Recolored repeated silhouette.
39:    - 2: Three readable variants with telegraphs and material cues.
40:    - 3: Varied family with animation, anticipation, and gameplay clarity.
41: 4. Rewards/interactables.
42:    - 0: Plain sphere/ring/token.
43:    - 1: Repeated object with simple glow.
44:    - 2: Two authored forms with idle/collect states and UI feedback.
45:    - 3: Desirable, animated, and clearly valued during motion.
46: 5. World/environment.
47:    - 0: Flat plane, empty arena, box skyline.
48:    - 1: Themed but sparse repeated blocks.
49:    - 2: Layered prop kit with foreground/midground/background and scale cues.
50:    - 3: Dense authored world that supports gameplay readability.
51: 6. Materials/textures.
52:    - 0: Flat colors.
53:    - 1: Basic roughness/metalness or emissive color.
54:    - 2: Shared material roles, procedural decals, trim, panel lines, wear/noise.
55:    - 3: Rich cohesive material language with measured texture/resource use.
56: 7. Lighting/render.
57:    - 0: Default lights or unreadable darkness.
58:    - 1: Fog/bloom used as main style.
59:    - 2: Intentional tone mapping, exposure, key/fill/rim, contact, depth.
60:    - 3: Cinematic but readable composition with disciplined post-processing.
61: 8. VFX/motion.
62:    - 0: None or random particles.
63:    - 1: Generic particles/trails.
64:    - 2: Event-driven VFX for boost, pickup, hit, fail, combo, shield, or spawn.
65:    - 3: High-impact effects that clarify gameplay and remain performant.
66: 9. UI/HUD.
67:    - 0: Debug text or missing UI.
68:    - 1: Generic stat-card dashboard.
69:    - 2: Genre-specific HUD states, meters/icons, responsive text fit.
70:    - 3: Cohesive game interface with strong hierarchy and polished transitions.
71: 10. Performance evidence.
72:    - 0: No metrics after visual changes.
73:    - 1: Informal "seems fine".
74:    - 2: Renderer counts, build/browser QA, desktop/mobile screenshots, and technical-art budget notes.
75:    - 3: Baseline/post metrics, bottleneck notes, budgets, optimized asset strategy, and VFX/readability tradeoffs.
76: 
77: ## Thresholds
78: 
79: Premium:
80: 
81: - Every category at least 2.
82: - Average at least 2.3.
83: - Desktop and mobile active-play screenshots captured when mobile is in scope.
84: - Renderer diagnostics reported after graphics changes.
85: 
86: Showcase:
87: 
88: - At least six categories score 3.
89: - No category below 2.
90: - Average at least 2.7.
91: - Performance evidence includes before/after or budget-aware notes.
92: 
93: ## Automatic Failures
94: 
95: Any of these prevents a premium/AAA/showcase claim:
96: 
97: - Active screenshot is primitive-dominant.
98: - Main world is mostly stretched boxes, flat planes, or a sparse arena.
99: - Hero asset is mostly default primitives plus glow.
100: - Obstacles or rewards are one repeated silhouette.
101: - HUD is mostly rectangular stat/debug cards.
102: - Fog, darkness, bloom, or particles hide missing authored geometry.
103: - UI overlaps the play path, clips text, or fails mobile safe areas.
104: - The game is not playable through real input.
105: - No active-play screenshot was captured.
106: - No renderer diagnostics were collected after major graphics work.
107: - No technical-art budget or imported/generated asset diagnostics were reported for premium graphics work.
108: 
109: ## Measured Evidence
110: 
111: Run the canvas inspector (`npm run inspect:canvas`, or `threejs-qa-release/scripts/inspect-threejs-canvas.mjs`) on desktop and mobile and cite its `metrics` and `renderBudget` blocks in the scorecard. The numbers are advisory signals, not gates, but they must be reported and low values must be explained rather than ignored:
112: 
113: - `colorEntropyBits` below ~3.0 or `dominantColorShare` above ~0.6 suggests a sparse, flat scene — supporting evidence against World/environment or Materials/textures scores above 2.
114: - `edgeDensity` below ~0.04 suggests primitive-dominant or empty framing — supporting evidence against World/environment and Hero/player scores above 2.
115: - `luminance.contrast` below ~60 suggests fog/darkness compression — supporting evidence against Lighting/render scores above 2.
116: - `renderBudget` rows over the tier budget require a documented tradeoff in the technical-art budget (see `references/technical-art.md`).
117: - Renderer diagnostics (calls, triangles, geometries, textures) back the Performance evidence category.
118: 
119: ## Fresh-Eyes Review
120: 
121: The builder must not be the only grader. For premium/AAA/showcase claims:
122: 
123: - If the runner supports subagents (Task tool or equivalent), spawn a reviewer with ONLY: the screenshots, this scorecard file, and the inspector metrics JSON. No build context, no prior scores. The reviewer must receive the COMPLETE capture set — every captured state, desktop and mobile — never a hand-picked subset; a curated selection can hide weak states or miss content the builder knows exists (capture states with the inspector's `--state` flag so nothing is gated behind live play). The reviewer fills the scorecard independently; reconcile by taking the lower score per category unless concrete evidence overturns it. Report both score sets.
124: - If subagents are unavailable, run an adversarial self-review before finalizing: for each category, write one sentence making the strongest case that the score is a 1, citing what is visible in the screenshot; only then assign the score. Include these sentences in the report.
125: 
126: ## Report Format
127: 
128: ```text
129: Visual scorecard:
130: - Art direction: before X / after Y - evidence:
131: - Hero/player: before X / after Y - evidence:
132: - Obstacles/enemies: before X / after Y - evidence:
133: - Rewards/interactables: before X / after Y - evidence:
134: - World/environment: before X / after Y - evidence:
135: - Materials/textures: before X / after Y - evidence:
136: - Lighting/render: before X / after Y - evidence:
137: - VFX/motion: before X / after Y - evidence:
138: - UI/HUD: before X / after Y - evidence:
139: - Performance evidence: before X / after Y - evidence:
140: Measured evidence: colorEntropyBits / edgeDensity / luminance.contrast /
141:   dominantColorShare per viewport, renderer diagnostics, render budget rows
142: Fresh-eyes review: subagent scores or adversarial self-review notes
143: Average:
144: Automatic failures remaining:
145: ```
146: 
147: If any category remains below threshold, state the exact next pass instead of declaring completion.

1: # Render, Lighting, And VFX Recipes
2: 
3: Use this after authored forms exist. Rendering polish cannot compensate for missing models, props, or readable gameplay silhouettes.
4: 
5: ## Renderer Setup
6: 
7: - Set `renderer.outputColorSpace = THREE.SRGBColorSpace`.
8: - Choose tone mapping deliberately. `ACESFilmicToneMapping` often works for cinematic stylized scenes; simpler tone mapping can be better for bright arcade readability.
9: - Tune exposure against active gameplay, not a static title view.
10: - Cap DPR, especially on mobile. Start around `Math.min(devicePixelRatio, 1.5 or 2)` and profile.
11: - Update renderer, camera, composer, and CSS UI dimensions on resize.
12: - Use a transparent or explicit background only when composition requires it.
13: 
14: ## Camera Composition
15: 
16: - Keep the next decision visible. The camera should show player, immediate threat/reward, and route.
17: - Add depth layers: foreground speed elements, playable midground, background scale cues.
18: - Use FOV and camera distance to communicate speed without hiding hazards.
19: - Use camera shake sparingly and clamp intensity.
20: - Add camera impulses for hits/near misses/boosts, then ease back quickly.
21: - Check mobile framing separately; vertical and narrow layouts often need different offsets.
22: 
23: ## Lighting Stack
24: 
25: Use a small readable stack:
26: 
27: - Key light: defines form and direction.
28: - Fill light: keeps gameplay objects legible.
29: - Rim/back light: separates player and hazards from background.
30: - Practical/emissive lights: authored beacons, engines, pickups, arena markers.
31: - Contact shadows or shadow blobs: ground important objects.
32: 
33: Avoid many unmeasured dynamic lights. Prefer baked-looking material/emissive cues, light cards, or small unlit decals for repeated signals.
34: 
35: ## Shadows And Contact
36: 
37: - Use shadows for hero/player, major hazards, and large world anchors.
38: - Use smaller shadow maps and limited shadow casters when profiling shows cost.
39: - Add cheap contact discs or transparent planes for pickups/hovering objects.
40: - Tune bias to avoid acne and peter-panning.
41: - Do not let shadows hide collision reads.
42: 
43: ## Materials
44: 
45: Define material roles with the material kit in `references/technical-art.md` (`MeshStandardMaterial` for most surfaces, `MeshPhysicalMaterial` only where the premium feature is visible). At render time:
46: 
47: - Prefer material contrast before post effects: matte vs glossy, metal vs plastic, transparent vs opaque, bright trim vs dark contact.
48: - Use emissive maps or small emissive parts for signals instead of making entire objects glow.
49: - Keep material roles matched across UI and world: danger, reward, shield, boost, objective.
50: 
51: ## Fog, Background, And Depth
52: 
53: - Fog should reveal depth and mood, not hide empty worlds.
54: - Layer background silhouettes at varied scales and heights.
55: - Add parallax or slow-moving far layers for motion-heavy games.
56: - Avoid single flat sky colors when the world needs scale; use gradients only as support, not the whole art direction.
57: - Keep hazards/rewards readable against fog and background values.
58: 
59: ## Post-Processing
60: 
61: Use post as a finishing pass:
62: 
63: - Bloom: only authored emissive elements, not all bright materials.
64: - Vignette: subtle focus, never heavy darkness.
65: - Film grain/noise: low opacity; avoid compression-like artifacts.
66: - Chromatic aberration: only brief event-driven impacts or very subtle style.
67: - Motion blur/trails: prefer geometry trails or particles that preserve gameplay clarity.
68: 
69: Always compare screenshots with post enabled/disabled and profile the cost.
70: 
71: ## Event-Driven VFX
72: 
73: Tie effects to state using the event-driven VFX language in `references/technical-art.md` (pickup, hit/fail, boost/speed, near miss/combo, shield/invulnerable, spawn/despawn). Pool effects, reuse geometries/materials, and keep permanent particle fields cheap and sparse.
74: 
75: ## Readability Checks
76: 
77: During active play, confirm:
78: 
79: - Player orientation is clear.
80: - Threats differ from rewards by both shape and material.
81: - Important pickups are visible before reaction time expires.
82: - UI feedback does not cover the play path.
83: - VFX clarifies state instead of obscuring collisions.
84: - Background contrast does not swallow dark objects.
85: 
86: ## Performance Checks
87: 
88: After render changes, report the renderer diagnostics from `references/technical-art.md` (calls, triangles, geometries, textures, materials, DPR/post/shadow settings), plus FPS/frame time and composer/post pass count when available.
89: 
90: If performance drops, reduce post/shadow cost first, then cull/LOD/instance, then reduce asset density only where it is least visible.

1: # Procedural Model Recipes
2: 
3: These recipes are for scratch-built Three.js models when external art assets are unavailable. The goal is not photorealism; it is authored, layered, readable, premium browser-game art.
4: 
5: ## Modeling Principles
6: 
7: - Start with silhouette. A model should be recognizable as a dark shape before materials or glow.
8: - Combine primitive bases with authored geometry: extrusions, bevels, curves, tubes, lathes, custom buffers, decals, trim, and instanced micro-detail.
9: - Use asymmetry and functional parts: hinges, fins, vents, handles, rails, brackets, sensors, cables, panels, bolts.
10: - Put detail where the camera sees it. Spend triangles on player-facing surfaces, not hidden undersides.
11: - Create state variants through material swaps, animated child parts, emissive strips, and VFX sockets.
12: - Keep a simple collision proxy separate from the detailed visual group.
13: - Use shared geometries/materials and instancing for repeated bolts, panels, lights, windows, spikes, rocks, or rail segments.
14: - Name important child meshes: `cockpitGlass`, `leftEngine`, `hazardTeeth`, `pickupCore`, `collisionProxy`.
15: 
16: ## Minimum Premium Asset Pass
17: 
18: For a game that asks for premium/AAA/showcase quality, build at least:
19: 
20: - One hero/player model with readable front/up/side and three state cues.
21: - Three obstacle/enemy variants with unique silhouettes and telegraphs.
22: - Two reward/interactable variants with idle and collect states.
23: - One world prop kit with at least eight reusable parts.
24: - One material kit with trim, decals, panel lines, and emissive masks.
25: - Collision proxies and renderer diagnostics for the above.
26: 
27: ## Hero Vehicle Recipe
28: 
29: Use for runners, racers, hovercraft, spaceships, drones, or arcade vehicles.
30: 
31: - Core hull: `ExtrudeGeometry` or custom tapered `BufferGeometry`, not just a box.
32: - Nose/front: wedge, intake, sensor strip, bumper, or blade shape.
33: - Cockpit/core: glass dome from sphere/lathe segments, beveled capsule, or faceted canopy.
34: - Engines: cylinders/cones/tubes with nozzle rings, inner emissive discs, heat fins, and trail sockets.
35: - Wings/fins: extruded triangular or curved plates with bevel/trim lines.
36: - Undercarriage: skids, landing pads, rail clamps, suspension arms, or thruster pods.
37: - Decals: panel lines, numeric marks, faction glyph, hazard ticks, small bolts.
38: - State cues: boost flares, shield shell, damage scorch, pickup glow, overheat red.
39: - Collision proxy: one capsule/box/sphere group matching gameplay footprint.
40: 
41: Reject if the hero is mostly a box with two cylinders and a glow.
42: 
43: ## Hero Character Recipe
44: 
45: Use for arena fighters, brawlers, platformers, or stylized third-person games.
46: 
47: - Body mass: torso, pelvis, head/helmet, limbs with tapered capsule/cylinder custom scales.
48: - Rig illusion: separate shoulders, elbows, knees, wrists, ankles, belt, backpack, armor plates.
49: - Face/identity: visor, mask, hair/helmet crest, color-blocked silhouette, weapon/tool.
50: - Animation-ready pivots: group limbs under named joints even if animation is procedural.
51: - Material zones: skin/fabric/armor/metal/glass/emissive accents.
52: - State cues: hit flash material, shield ring, attack trail socket, stamina/charge glow.
53: - Collision proxy: capsule or cylinder independent of mesh detail.
54: 
55: Reject if the character reads as stacked spheres/cylinders with no costume, joints, or silhouette.
56: 
57: ## Obstacle And Enemy Families
58: 
59: Build distinct gameplay reads:
60: 
61: - Low barrier: ground-hugging slab, spikes, rails, caution panels, animated warning light.
62: - Gate/arch: overhead frame, side posts, pulsing pass/avoid lane, moving shutters.
63: - Moving hazard: rotating arm, sweeper beam, drone, crusher, sliding block, orbiting mines.
64: - Trap/zone: laser grid, electric puddle, collapsing tile, gravity well, proximity mine.
65: - Enemy: body core, sensor/head, weapon, shield, locomotion/hover base, attack telegraph.
66: 
67: Each variant needs:
68: 
69: - Unique silhouette.
70: - Material cue for danger.
71: - Telegraph from distance.
72: - Animation or state change.
73: - Collision proxy.
74: - Low-cost repeated detail.
75: 
76: Reject if all hazards are recolored cubes/cones.
77: 
78: ## Reward And Interactable Recipes
79: 
80: Rewards should be readable and desirable during motion.
81: 
82: - Token: outer ring, inner core, value icon, shimmer cards, collect burst socket.
83: - Shard: faceted crystal, metal bracket, orbiting chips, emissive seam.
84: - Capsule: glass shell, suspended item, end caps, rotating label strip.
85: - Power-up: icon silhouette matched to effect, color and shape differ from score pickups.
86: - Objective item: larger scale, unique motion, UI echo, stronger lighting/VFX.
87: 
88: States:
89: 
90: - Idle: slow rotation, pulse, bob, or orbit.
91: - Attract: line/trail toward player.
92: - Collect: vanish, burst, score trail, HUD meter update.
93: 
94: Reject if rewards are plain spheres or torus rings without state feedback.
95: 
96: ## World Prop Kit
97: 
98: Build modular props that can be instanced and recombined:
99: 
100: - Track/road: lane plates, seams, arrows, side rails, guard segments, repair panels.
101: - Arena: boundary rings, floor tiles, spawn pads, cover blocks, goal markers.
102: - City/sci-fi: window strips, antennas, rooftop units, bridge trusses, pylons, billboards.
103: - Nature: rocks from custom faceted buffers, cliffs, roots, crystals, grasses as cards.
104: - Industrial: pipes, vents, cables, tanks, crates, gantries, lights, warning signs.
105: - Space/air: debris panels, satellites, buoys, asteroid chunks, parallax dust.
106: 
107: Layer the kit:
108: 
109: - Near props create speed and scale.
110: - Mid props define the playable corridor.
111: - Far props create depth without stealing draw calls.
112: 
113: Reject if the world is mostly stretched boxes or a flat plane.
114: 
115: ## Procedural Geometry Techniques
116: 
117: - `ExtrudeGeometry`: panels, fins, wings, badges, UI/world glyphs, signs.
118: - `LatheGeometry`: capsules, domes, engines, pipes, bottles, turret bases.
119: - `TubeGeometry`: cables, rails, trails, conduits, curved weapons.
120: - Custom `BufferGeometry`: tapered hulls, rocks, shards, wedges, low-poly terrain.
121: - `ShapeGeometry`: decals, flat icons, trim strips, hazard markers.
122: - `InstancedMesh`: windows, bolts, lane markers, debris, grass, lights, small props.
123: - `LOD`: hero/background variants and dense prop reductions.
124: 
125: Use bevel-like layering when real bevel geometry is too expensive: duplicate thin trim meshes, edge strips, or slightly offset darker panels.
126: 
127: ## Material And Detail Rules
128: 
129: - Use roughness/metalness contrast, not only hue contrast.
130: - Use emissive for authored signals, not entire objects.
131: - Use glass/clearcoat sparingly on hero details.
132: - Add darker contact material under important objects.
133: - Use decals to imply scale and function.
134: - Reuse UI icon shapes as world decals for cohesion.
135: 
136: ## Diagnostics Checklist
137: 
138: After a model pass, report:
139: 
140: - Mesh count.
141: - Instanced mesh count.
142: - Unique geometries/materials/textures.
143: - Approximate triangle count if available.
144: - Collision proxies included.
145: - LOD or culling strategy for repeated/background props.
146: - Active-play screenshots, not only showroom renders.

(End of file - total 146 lines)
</content>

18: // WHY: monta o mundo do jogo (tudo que não depende do loop)

41: // WHY: tela de menu/fim — texto central no canvas do HUD
42: const drawOverlay = (ctx, w, h, title, sub) => {
43:   // WHY: clearRect antes do fundo — evita ghosting do overlay anterior no canvas 2D
44:   ctx.clearRect(0, 0, w, h);
45:   ctx.fillStyle = 'rgba(0,0,0,0.72)';
46:   ctx.fillRect(0, 0, w, h);
47:   ctx.fillStyle = '#ffcc33';
48:   ctx.font = 'bold 28px monospace';
49:   ctx.textAlign = 'center';
50:   ctx.fillText(title, w / 2, h / 2 - 10);
51:   ctx.fillStyle = '#fff';
52:   ctx.font = '14px monospace';
53:   ctx.fillText(sub, w / 2, h / 2 + 20);
54: };

56: // WHY: liga update/render/estados ao loop fixed-step do Game
57: const wire = (w) => {
58:   buildWorld(w.engine.world, w.level.grid);
59:   const enemyMeshes = buildEnemyMeshes(w.engine.world, w.enemies);
60:   const viewmodel = buildViewmodel(w.engine.camera);
61:   const { camera, renderer, scene } = w.engine;
62:   let lastHp = w.player.hp;
63:   w.projectiles = [];

65:   // WHY: splash do foguete — dano a todos os inimigos na área (não ao player)
66:   const splashDamage = (x, z, radius, damage) => {
67:     for (const e of w.enemies) {

70:       if (d <= radius) e.damage(damage);

78:       dir: { x: dir.x, z: dir.z },

82:   };

86:     w.__updates = (w.__updates ?? 0) + 1; // WHY: contador p/ profiling fixed-step (E2E)

91:       if (evt && evt.damage > 0) {

94:           knockback(w.player.vel, evt.from.x - w.player.pos.x, evt.from.z - w.player.pos.z, 2.5);
95:         } else if (evt.type === 'hitscan') {
96:           w.player.damage(evt.damage);
97:         } else if (evt.type === 'double') {
98:           const a = { x: evt.dir.x, z: evt.dir.z };
99:           const rot = (s) => ({ x: a.x * Math.cos(s) - a.z * Math.sin(s), z: a.x * Math.sin(s) + a.z * Math.cos(s) });
100:           pushProjectile(evt.from, rot(0.12), evt.speed ?? 6, evt.damage, 'enemy');
101:           pushProjectile(evt.from, rot(-0.12), evt.speed ?? 6, evt.damage, 'enemy');

104:         }

107:       if (e.dead && !e.scored) { e.scored = true; w.score += 10; }

7:   enemyShoot: { type: 'sawtooth', freq: 220, dur: 0.1, slide: -80 },

10:   door: { type: 'square', freq: 90, dur: 0.2, slide: -30 },
11:   explosion: { type: 'sawtooth', freq: 120, dur: 0.35, slide: -90 },
12: };

14: class AudioEngine {
15:   constructor(ctx = null) {
16:     this.ctx = ctx;
17:     this.muted = false;
18:     this.lastPlayed = null;
19:     this.queue = [];
20:     this.musicPlaying = false;
21:   }
22: 
23:   // WHY: cria o contexto sob demanda (autoplay policy do browser exige gesto do usuário)
24:   ensureCtx() {
25:     if (this.ctx) return this.ctx;
26:     if (typeof window !== 'undefined' && window.AudioContext) {
27:       this.ctx = new window.AudioContext();
28:     }
29:     return this.ctx;
30:   }
31: 
32:   play(name) {
33:     this.lastPlayed = name;
34:     this.queue.push(name);
35:     const s = SOUNDS[name];
36:     if (!s) return false;
37:     const ctx = this.ensureCtx();
38:     if (!ctx || this.muted) return false;
39:     const osc = ctx.createOscillator();
40:     const gain = ctx.createGain();
41:     osc.type = s.type;
42:     osc.frequency.setValueAtTime(s.freq, ctx.currentTime);
43:     osc.frequency.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(Math.max(30, s.freq + s.slide), ctx.currentTime + s.dur);
44:     gain.gain.setValueAtTime(0.15, ctx.currentTime);
45:     gain.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.001, ctx.currentTime + s.dur);
46:     osc.connect(gain).connect(ctx.destination);
47:     osc.start(ctx.currentTime);
48:     osc.stop(ctx.currentTime + s.dur);
49:     return true;
50:   }

5:   applyFriction,

10: } from './move.js';

12: const { floor, min, max } = Math;

14: class PlayerEntity {
15:   constructor(level, input, weapons) {
16:     const s = level.playerSpawn;
17:     // WHY: centro do tile (spawn.x/z são índices inteiros do grid)
18:     this.pos = { x: s.x + 0.5, z: s.z + 0.5 };
19:     this.y = 0;
20:     this.vel = { x: 0, z: 0, y: 0 };
21:     this.yaw = s.yaw ?? -Math.PI / 2;
22:     this.pitch = 0;
23:     this.hp = C.PLAYER.startHp;
24:     this.armor = C.PLAYER.startArmor;
25:     this.onGround = true;
26:     this.state = 'MENU'; // FSM: MENU -> PLAYING
27:     this.bobTime = 0;
28:     this.input = input;
29:     this.weapons = weapons;
30:     this.level = level;
31:   }
32: 
33:   // WHY: FSM — transições explícitas (lição 5: compare uppercase, comente cada transição)
34:   start() { this.state = 'PLAYING'; }
35:   pause() { this.state = 'MENU'; }
36: 
37:   isMoving() {
38:     return Math.abs(this.vel.x) > 0.05 || Math.abs(this.vel.z) > 0.05;
39:   }
40: 
41:   update(dt) {
42:     if (this.state !== 'PLAYING') return;
43:     // WHY: cooldown das armas avança com o tempo de jogo (W8 — sem isso o browser
44:     // nunca decrementava o cooldown e canFire() ficava false após o 1º tiro)
45:     this.weapons.update(dt);
46:     const wish = this.input.getAxis();
47:     const yaw = this.input.yaw;
48: 
49:     // WHY: R_y(-yaw) — câmera usa rotation.y = -yaw, então frente = (sin yaw, -cos yaw);
50:     // R_y(+yaw) deixava W/S invertidos em relação à câmera (bug "teclas WS invertidas")
51:     const wishX = -wish.z * Math.sin(yaw) + wish.x * Math.cos(yaw);
52:     const wishZ = wish.z * Math.cos(yaw) + wish.x * Math.sin(yaw);
53: 
54:     const speed = this.input.isDown('ShiftLeft') ? C.PHYSICS.runSpeed : C.PHYSICS.walkSpeed;
55:     accelerate(this.vel, { x: wishX, z: wishZ }, C.PHYSICS.accel * speed, dt);
56:     applyFriction(this.vel, dt, this.onGround);
57:     if (this.input.isDown('Space')) tryJump(this.vel, this.onGround);
58:     applyGravity(this.vel, dt);
59: 
60:     // WHY: colisão horizontal por eixo — moveAxis usa pos {x,y} do grid 2D,
61:     // então traduzimos para {x: col, y: row} e de volta para pos {x,z}
62:     const gp = { x: this.pos.x, y: this.pos.z };
63:     const rX = moveAxis(gp, { x: this.vel.x, y: this.vel.z }, 'x', dt, this.level.grid, C.PLAYER.radius);
64:     const rZ = moveAxis(rX.pos, { x: rX.vel.x, y: rX.vel.y }, 'y', dt, this.level.grid, C.PLAYER.radius);
65:     this.pos.x = rZ.pos.x;
66:     this.pos.z = rZ.pos.y;
67:     this.vel.x = rZ.vel.x;
68:     this.vel.z = rZ.vel.y;
69: 
70:     // WHY: altura vertical — chão em y=0, sem teto no mapa
71:     this.y += this.vel.y * dt;
72:     if (this.y <= 0) {
73:       this.y = 0;
74:       this.vel.y = 0;
75:       this.onGround = true;
76:     } else if (this.vel.y !== 0) {
77:       this.onGround = false;
78:     }
79: 
80:     if (this.isMoving()) this.bobTime += dt;
81:     this.yaw = yaw;
82:     this.pitch = this.input.pitch;
83: 
84:     this.stepHazards(dt);
85:     this.collectPickups();
86:   }
87: 
88:   // WHY: lava causa dano contínuo (tile LAVA do grid)
89:   // WHY: guard de bounds — se o player sair do grid (knockback extremo), grid[z] é
90:   // undefined e `undefined[x]` lançaria TypeError, matando o rAF (jogo congela)
91:   stepHazards(dt) {
92:     const row = this.level.grid[floor(this.pos.z)];
93:     const tile = row ? row[floor(this.pos.x)] : undefined;
94:     if (tile === C.TILES.LAVA) this.damage(12 * dt);
95:   }
96: 
97:   collectPickups() {
98:     const remaining = [];
99:     for (const p of this.level.pickups) {
100:       const d = Math.hypot(p.x + 0.5 - this.pos.x, p.z + 0.5 - this.pos.z);
101:       if (d < 0.6) {
102:         if (p.type === C.TILES.HEALTH) this.hp = min(C.PLAYER.startHp, this.hp + 25);
103:         else if (p.type === C.TILES.ARMOR) this.armor = min(100, this.armor + 25);
104:         // WHY: W9 — pickup W desbloqueia arma nova (shotgun → rocket) e SEMPRE dá
105:         // munição; antes só dava munição e o inventário já vinha completo (DOOM clássico)
106:         else if (p.type === C.TILES.WEAPON) {
107:           if (!this.weapons.inventory.includes('shotgun')) this.weapons.unlockWeapon('shotgun');
108:           else if (!this.weapons.inventory.includes('rocket')) this.weapons.unlockWeapon('rocket');
109:           this.weapons.addAmmo('all', 20);
110:         }
111:       } else {
112:         remaining.push(p);
113:       }
114:     }
115:     this.level.pickups = remaining;
116:   }
117: 
118:   // WHY: armadura absorve 50% do dano antes do HP (DOOM clássico)
119:   // WHY: sem Math.round — dano contínuo (lava 12*dt com dt<1/12) seria anulado
120:   damage(amount) {
121:     if (this.armor > 0) {
122:       const absorbed = min(this.armor, amount * 0.5);
123:       this.armor -= absorbed;
124:       amount -= absorbed;
125:     }
126:     this.hp = max(0, this.hp - amount);
127:     return this.hp;
128:   }
129: 
130:   viewY() {
131:     return C.PLAYER.height + cameraBob(this.bobTime, this.isMoving(), 1).y;
132:   }
133: }
134: 
135: export { PlayerEntity };

1: // js/hud.js — W6: painel retro Canvas2D (barras HP/armor, ammo, weapon slot, score, crosshair)
2: // Dados puros + render com ctx injetado (testável em node)
3: 
4: // WHY: cores do painel retro — verde HP, azul armadura (DOOM clássico)
5: const COLORS = {
6:   hp: '#33ff33',
7:   armor: '#3366ff',
8:   ammo: '#ffcc33',
9:   bg: 'rgba(16,16,20,0.85)',
10:   text: '#fff',
11:   barBg: '#111',
12:   cross: '#ccffcc',
13: };
14: 
15: const WEAPON_NAMES = { fist: 'FIST', pistol: 'PISTOL', shotgun: 'SHOTGUN', rocket: 'ROCKET' };
16: 
17: // WHY: dados puros do HUD — testável sem canvas
18: // WHY: weapon/ammo via weapons.key (nome) — current é ÍNDICE do inventário e
19: // ammo[current] retornava undefined (HUD mostrava "1 undefined" em vez de "PISTOL 50")
20: const buildHudData = (player, weapons) => {
21:   const key = weapons.key ?? weapons.current;
22:   return {
23:     hp: Math.max(0, Math.round(player.hp ?? 0)),
24:     maxHp: player.maxHp ?? 100,
25:     armor: Math.max(0, Math.round(player.armor ?? 0)),
26:     maxArmor: player.maxArmor ?? 100,
27:     weapon: key,
28:     ammo: weapons.ammo[key],
29:     score: player.score ?? 0,
30:   };
31: };
32: 
33: // WHY: render do painel (ctx injetado; w/h = dimensões do canvas)
34: const renderHud = (ctx, data, w, h) => {
35:   const pad = 16;
36:   const barW = 132;
37:   const barH = 9;
38: 
39:   // WHY: clearRect — sem limpar, o fundo escuro do menu (drawOverlay) fica retido
40:   // no canvas 2D cobrindo a cena 3D (bug "após start tudo preto")
41:   ctx.clearRect(0, 0, w, h);
42: 
43:   // painel inferior
44:   ctx.fillStyle = COLORS.bg;
45:   ctx.fillRect(0, h - 26, w, 26);
46: 
47:   // barra HP (verde) — fundo + preenchimento proporcional
48:   ctx.fillStyle = COLORS.barBg;
49:   ctx.fillRect(pad, h - 21, barW, barH);
50:   ctx.fillStyle = COLORS.hp;
51:   ctx.fillRect(pad, h - 21, barW * Math.min(1, data.hp / data.maxHp), barH);
52: 
53:   // barra armor (azul)
54:   ctx.fillStyle = COLORS.barBg;
55:   ctx.fillRect(pad, h - 10, barW, barH);
56:   ctx.fillStyle = COLORS.armor;
57:   ctx.fillRect(pad, h - 10, barW * Math.min(1, data.armor / data.maxArmor), barH);
58: 
59:   // ammo + weapon slot (canto direito)
60:   ctx.fillStyle = COLORS.ammo;
61:   ctx.font = '14px monospace';
62:   ctx.textAlign = 'right';
63:   const ammoStr = data.ammo === Infinity ? '∞' : data.ammo;
64:   ctx.fillText(`${WEAPON_NAMES[data.weapon] ?? data.weapon} ${ammoStr}`, w - pad, h - 8);
65: 
66:   // score (acima do painel)
67:   ctx.fillStyle = COLORS.text;
68:   ctx.textAlign = 'left';
69:   ctx.fillText(`SCORE ${data.score}`, pad, h - 32);
70: 
71:   // crosshair (+ no centro)
72:   const cx = w / 2;
73:   const cy = h / 2;
74:   ctx.strokeStyle = COLORS.cross;
75:   ctx.lineWidth = 2;

1: // js/move.js — física pura para DOOM clone
2: // Sem dependências, testável em node
3: 
4: import C from './constants.js';
5: import { R_y, clamp } from './utils.js';
6: 
7: // WHY: aplica gravidade ao vetor de velocidade (clamp só no limite inferior — não corta pulo)
8: const applyGravity = (vel, dt) => {
9:   vel.y += C.PHYSICS.gravity * dt;
10:   if (vel.y < C.PHYSICS.maxFall) vel.y = C.PHYSICS.maxFall;
11:   return vel;
12: };
13: 
14: // WHY: aplica atrito ou resistência do ar
15: const applyFriction = (vel, dt, onGround) => {
16:   if (onGround) {
17:     vel.x *= 1 - C.PHYSICS.friction * dt;
18:     vel.z *= 1 - C.PHYSICS.friction * dt;
19:   } else {
20:     vel.x *= 1 - C.PHYSICS.airResist * dt;
21:     vel.z *= 1 - C.PHYSICS.airResist * dt;
22:   }
23:   return vel;
24: };
25: 
26: // WHY: acelera o jogador na direção desejada
27: const accelerate = (vel, wishdir, accel, dt) => {
28:   vel.x += wishdir.x * accel * dt;
29:   vel.z += wishdir.z * accel * dt;
30:   return vel;
31: };
32: 
33: // WHY: move e resolve colisão AABB por eixo — checa a área varrida inteira
34: const moveAxis = (pos, vel, axis, dt, grid, radius) => {
35:   const newVel = { ...vel };
36:   const newPos = { ...pos };
37: 
38:   // WHY: eixo complementar (y é o eixo "outro" nos testes 2D)
39:   const other = axis === 'x' ? 'y' : 'x';
40:   const oldMain = pos[axis];
41:   const oldOther = pos[other];
42:   const newMain = oldMain + vel[axis] * dt;
43:   const newOther = oldOther + vel[other] * dt;
44: 
45:   // WHY: faixa varrida pelo AABB do centro antigo ao novo (+radius)
46:   const lo = Math.floor(Math.min(oldMain, newMain) - radius);
47:   const hi = Math.floor(Math.max(oldMain, newMain) + radius);
48:   const oLo = Math.floor(oldOther - radius);
49:   const oHi = Math.floor(newOther + radius);
50: 
51:   // WHY: fora do grid = parede (nunca `grid[r][c]` com r/c fora — isso lançaria
52:   // TypeError e mataria o rAF; o knockback do W9 empurra o player até a borda)
53:   const isWall = (r, c) => r < 0 || r >= grid.length || c < 0 || c >= grid[0].length || grid[r][c] === C.TILES.WALL;
54:   let collided = false;
55:   for (let a = lo; a <= hi && !collided; a++) {
56:     for (let b = oLo; b <= oHi; b++) {
57:       const cell = axis === 'x' ? isWall(b, a) : isWall(a, b);
58:       if (cell) { collided = true; break; }
59:     }
60:   }
61: 
62:   if (collided) {
63:     newVel[axis] = 0;
64:     newPos[axis] = oldMain;
65:   } else {
66:     newPos[axis] = newMain;
67:     newPos[other] = newOther;
68:   }
69: 
70:   return { pos: newPos, vel: newVel, collided };
71: };
72: 
73: // WHY: aplica pulo quando no chão
74: const tryJump = (vel, onGround) => {
75:   if (onGround) vel.y = C.PHYSICS.jumpVel;
76:   return vel;
77: };
78: 
79: // WHY: aplica knockback ao jogador
80: const knockback = (vel, dirX, dirZ, force) => {
81:   vel.x += dirX * force * C.PHYSICS.BOUNCE;
82:   vel.z += dirZ * force * C.PHYSICS.BOUNCE;
83:   return vel;
84: };
85: 
86: // WHY: calcula dano de splash por distância
87: const splashDamage = (damage, dist, radius) => {
88:   if (dist > radius) return 0;
89:   if (dist === 0) return damage;
90:   return damage * (1 - dist / radius);
91: };
92: 
93: // WHY: bobbing da câmera
94: const cameraBob = (time, moving, speed) => {
95:   const bobAmp = C.PHYSICS.bobAmp;
96:   const bobFreq = C.PHYSICS.bobFreq;
97:   if (!moving) return { x: 0, y: 0 };
98:   return {
99:     x: Math.sin(time * bobFreq) * bobAmp,
100:     y: Math.sin(time * bobFreq * 2) * bobAmp * 0.5,
101:   };
102: };
103: 
104: export {
105:   applyGravity,
106:   applyFriction,
107:   accelerate,
108:   moveAxis,
109:   tryJump,
110:   knockback,
111:   splashDamage,
112:   cameraBob,
113: };

1: // js/weapons.js — WeaponSystem (W3): Fist, Pistol, Shotgun, Rocket + munição
2: import C from './constants.js';
3: import { hasLineOfSight } from './map.js';
4: 
5: const { floor, min, hypot } = Math;
6: 
7: // WHY: slots fixos de arma (teclas 1-4) — o inventário é desbloqueável (W9)
8: const SLOTS = ['fist', 'pistol', 'shotgun', 'rocket'];
9: 
10: // WHY: raycast DDA contra o grid (hitscan/spread) — retorna ponto de impacto
11: const raycast = (player, grid, spread = 0) => {
12:   const yaw = player.yaw + (Math.random() - 0.5) * 2 * spread;
13:   const dx = Math.sin(yaw);
14:   const dz = Math.cos(yaw);
15:   let x = player.pos.x;
16:   let z = player.pos.z;
17:   let dist = 0;
18:   while (dist < 60) {
19:     x += dx * 0.05;
20:     z += dz * 0.05;
21:     dist += 0.05;
22:     const tx = floor(x);
23:     const tz = floor(z);
24:     if (tx < 0 || tz < 0 || tx >= C.MAP.gridW || tz >= C.MAP.gridH) break;
25:     const tile = grid[tz][tx];
26:     if (tile === C.TILES.WALL || tile === C.TILES.DOOR) {
27:       return { x, z, dist, hit: true, tile };
28:     }
29:   }
30:   return { x, z, dist, hit: false, tile: null };
31: };
32: 
33: class WeaponSystem {
34:   constructor() {
35:     // WHY: inventário começa só com fist+pistol; shotgun/rocket são desbloqueados
36:     // pelos pickups W (DOOM clássico — antes todas as 4 armas já vinham "equipadas",
37:     // então "armas não apareciam" e o pickup W só dava munição)
38:     this.inventory = ['fist', 'pistol'];
39:     this.current = 0;
40:     this.ammo = { fist: Infinity, pistol: 50, shotgun: 12, rocket: 4 };
41:     this.cooldown = 0;
42:   }
43: 
44:   get weapon() { return C.WEAPON[this.inventory[this.current]]; }
45:   get name() { return this.weapon.name; }
46:   get key() { return this.inventory[this.current]; }
47: 
48:   // WHY: desbloqueia arma (pickup W) e equipa automaticamente (DOOM clássico)
49:   unlockWeapon(key) {
50:     if (!C.WEAPON[key]) return false;
51:     if (!this.inventory.includes(key)) {
52:       this.inventory.push(key);
53:       this.current = this.inventory.length - 1;
54:     }
55:     return true;
56:   }
57: 
58:   update(dt) {
59:     this.cooldown = Math.max(0, this.cooldown - dt);
60:   }
61: 
62:   canFire() {
63:     const w = this.weapon;
64:     return this.cooldown <= 0 && (this.key === 'fist' || this.ammo[this.key] >= w.ammoCost);
65:   }
66: 
67:   // WHY: switch por SLOT fixo (1-4) — arma não-desbloqueada não troca (W9)
68:   switchWeapon(slot) {
69:     const key = SLOTS[slot];
70:     if (key && this.inventory.includes(key)) this.current = this.inventory.indexOf(key);
71:   }
72: 
73:   // WHY: tipo 'all' distribui munição para todas as armas de munição (pickup W)
74:   addAmmo(type, qty) {
75:     if (type === 'all') {
76:       for (const k of ['pistol', 'shotgun', 'rocket']) {
77:         this.ammo[k] = min(C.WEAPON[k].maxAmmo, this.ammo[k] + qty);
78:       }
79:       return;
80:     }
81:     if (!C.WEAPON[type]) return;
82:     this.ammo[type] = min(C.WEAPON[type].maxAmmo, this.ammo[type] + qty);
83:   }
84: 
85:   fire(player, grid) {
86:     if (!this.canFire()) return null;
87:     const w = this.weapon;
88:     const key = this.key;
89:     this.cooldown = w.rate;
90:     if (key !== 'fist') this.ammo[key] -= w.ammoCost;
91: 
92:     switch (w.type) {
93:       case 'melee':
94:         return { type: 'melee', weapon: key, damage: w.damage, range: w.range };
95:       case 'hitscan':
96:         return { type: 'hitscan', weapon: key, damage: w.damage, hit: raycast(player, grid) };
97:       case 'spread': {
98:         const pellets = [];
99:         for (let i = 0; i < w.pellets; i++) pellets.push(raycast(player, grid, w.spread));
100:         return { type: 'spread', weapon: key, damage: w.damage, pellets };
101:       }
102:       case 'projectile':
103:         return {
104:           type: 'projectile',
105:           weapon: key,
106:           damage: w.damage,
107:           splash: w.splash,
108:           proj: {
109:             x: player.pos.x,
110:             z: player.pos.z,
111:             y: player.viewY ? 1.0 : 1.0,
112:             dx: Math.sin(player.yaw),
113:             dz: Math.cos(player.yaw),
114:             speed: 14,
115:             dist: 0,
116:           },
117:         };
118:       default:
119:         return null;
120:     }
121:   }
122: }
123: 
124: // WHY: inimigo mais próximo na linha de tiro (hitscan/spread) — W9: antes o tiro
125: // só colidia com o grid e nunca acertava inimigos (jogo injogável)
126: // WHY: frente = (sin yaw, -cos yaw) — convenção R_y(-yaw) dos testes de movimento
127: const raycastEnemy = (player, grid, enemies, maxDist, doors = []) => {
128:   const dirX = Math.sin(player.yaw);
129:   const dirZ = -Math.cos(player.yaw);
130:   let best = null;
131:   let bestAlong = Infinity;
132:   for (const e of enemies) {
133:     if (e.dead) continue;
134:     const dx = e.pos.x - player.pos.x;
135:     const dz = e.pos.z - player.pos.z;
136:     const along = dx * dirX + dz * dirZ;
137:     if (along <= 0 || along > maxDist) continue;
138:     // WHY: distância perpendicular ao raio — acerta se o centro está a < size*0.5 do raio
139:     const perp = Math.abs(dx * dirZ - dz * dirX);
140:     if (perp > e.stats.size * 0.5) continue;
141:     if (!hasLineOfSight(grid, player.pos.x, player.pos.z, e.pos.x, e.pos.z, doors)) continue;
142:     if (along < bestAlong) { best = e; bestAlong = along; }
143:   }
144:   return best;
145: };
146: 
147: // WHY: inimigo mais próximo dentro do alcance melee (dano por proximidade — DOOM)
148: const meleeTarget = (player, enemies, range) => {
149:   let best = null;
150:   let bestDist = range;
151:   for (const e of enemies) {
152:     if (e.dead) continue;
153:     const d = hypot(e.pos.x - player.pos.x, e.pos.z - player.pos.z);
154:     if (d <= bestDist) { bestDist = d; best = e; }
155:   }
156:   return best;
157: };
158: 
159: export { WeaponSystem, raycast, raycastEnemy, meleeTarget };

(End of file - total 159 lines)
</content>

1: // js/particles.js — W5: sistema de partículas (explosões, sangue, sparkles)
2: // Dados puros + render Canvas2D com ctx injetado (testável em node)
3: 
4: // WHY: converte 0xRRGGBB para css (#rrggbb) — canvas precisa string
5: const hexToCss = (n) => `#${n.toString(16).padStart(6, '0')}`;
6: 
7: class Particle {
8:   constructor(x, z, y = 0.5, opts = {}) {
9:     this.x = x;
10:     this.z = z;
11:     this.y = y;
12:     this.vx = opts.vx ?? 0;
13:     this.vz = opts.vz ?? 0;
14:     this.vy = opts.vy ?? 0;
15:     this.life = opts.life ?? 0.6;
16:     this.maxLife = this.life;
17:     this.color = opts.color ?? 0xffaa33;
18:     this.size = opts.size ?? 0.1;
19:     this.gravity = opts.gravity ?? 0;
20:   }
21: 
22:   get alive() { return this.life > 0; }
23: 
24:   update(dt) {
25:     this.life -= dt;
26:     if (!this.alive) return;
27:     this.vy += this.gravity * dt;
28:     this.x += this.vx * dt;
29:     this.z += this.vz * dt;
30:     this.y += this.vy * dt;
31:   }
32: }
33: 
34: class ParticleSystem {
35:   constructor() { this.particles = []; }
36: 
37:   get aliveCount() { return this.particles.filter((p) => p.alive).length; }
38: 
39:   spawn(x, z, y, opts) { this.particles.push(new Particle(x, z, y, opts)); }
40: 
41:   // WHY: explosão radial com velocidade aleatória (fireball estilo DOOM)
42:   explosion(x, z, y = 0.5, count = 12, power = 3) {
43:     for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
44:       const a = Math.random() * Math.PI * 2;
45:       const v = power * (0.3 + Math.random() * 0.7);
46:       this.spawn(x, z, y, {
47:         vx: Math.cos(a) * v, vz: Math.sin(a) * v, vy: Math.random() * 2,
48:         life: 0.4 + Math.random() * 0.4, color: 0xff8800, size: 0.15, gravity: -6,
49:       });
50:     }
51:   }
52: 
53:   blood(x, z, y = 0.5, count = 8) {
54:     for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
55:       const a = Math.random() * Math.PI * 2;
56:       const v = 1 + Math.random();
57:       this.spawn(x, z, y, {
58:         vx: Math.cos(a) * v, vz: Math.sin(a) * v, vy: Math.random(),
59:         life: 0.5, color: 0xcc2222, size: 0.08, gravity: -4,
60:       });
61:     }
62:   }
63: 
64:   spark(x, z, y = 0.5, count = 5) {
65:     for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
66:       const a = Math.random() * Math.PI * 2;
67:       const v = 2 + Math.random() * 2;
68:       this.spawn(x, z, y, {
69:         vx: Math.cos(a) * v, vz: Math.sin(a) * v, vy: Math.random() * 2,
70:         life: 0.2, color: 0xffdd44, size: 0.05,
71:       });
72:     }
73:   }
74: 
75:   update(dt) {
76:     for (const p of this.particles) p.update(dt);
77:     // WHY: remove mortos (compactação in-place — mantém aliveCount fiel)
78:     this.particles = this.particles.filter((p) => p.alive);
79:   }
80: 
81:   render(ctx, scale = 1) {
82:     for (const p of this.particles) {
83:       ctx.fillStyle = hexToCss(p.color);
84:       ctx.globalAlpha = Math.max(0, p.life / p.maxLife);
85:       ctx.fillRect((p.x - p.size) * scale, (p.z - p.size) * scale, p.size * 2 * scale, p.size * 2 * scale);
86:     }
87:     ctx.globalAlpha = 1;
88:   }
89: }
90:

1: // js/game.js — W6: game loop fixed-step 60Hz + máquina de estados
2: // rAF injetável (browser real ou stub de teste); step() síncrono testável
3: 
4: const FIXED_DT = 1 / 60;
5: const MAX_FRAME = 0.25; // clamp contra tab switch (dt em segundos)
6: 
7: const STATES = { MENU: 'MENU', PLAYING: 'PLAYING', PAUSED: 'PAUSED', GAMEOVER: 'GAMEOVER', WIN: 'WIN' };
8: 
9: class Game {
10:   constructor({ update, render, requestFrame = null }) {
11:     this.update = update;
12:     this.render = render;
13:     // WHY: requestFrame injetável — browser usa rAF; testes usam stub/step direto
14:     this.requestFrame = requestFrame ?? ((cb) => {
15:       if (typeof window !== 'undefined' && window.requestAnimationFrame) window.requestAnimationFrame(cb);
16:     });
17:     this.state = STATES.MENU;
18:     this.time = 0;
19:     this.acc = 0;
20:     this.last = 0;
21:     this.frame = 0;
22:     this.running = false;
23:   }
24: 
25:   start() {
26:     if (this.running) return;
27:     this.running = true;
28:     this.last = performance.now();
29:     this.frame = 0;
30:     const loop = (now) => {
31:       if (!this.running) return;
32:       this.step(now);
33:       this.requestFrame(loop);
34:     };
35:     this.requestFrame(loop);
36:   }
37: 
38:   stop() { this.running = false; }
39: 
40:   // WHY: passo síncrono — acumula dt real e processa N passos fixos de 1/60
41:   step(now) {
42:     if (!this.running) return;
43:     const dt = Math.min(Math.max((now - this.last) / 1000, 0), MAX_FRAME);
44:     this.last = now;
45:     this.acc += dt;
46:     while (this.acc >= FIXED_DT) {
47:       this.update(FIXED_DT);
48:       this.time += FIXED_DT;
49:       this.acc -= FIXED_DT;
50:       this.frame += 1;
51:     }
52:     this.render();
53:   }
54: 
55:   // WHY: transições de estado (Menu→Play→Pause→GameOver/Win)
56:   startGame() { this.state = STATES.PLAYING; }
57:   pause() { if (this.state === STATES.PLAYING) this.state = STATES.PAUSED; }
58:   resume() { if (this.state === STATES.PAUSED) this.state = STATES.PLAYING; }
59:   togglePause() { if (this.state === STATES.PLAYING) this.pause(); else if (this.state === STATES.PAUSED) this.resume(); }
60:   gameOver() { this.state = STATES.GAMEOVER; }
61:   win() { this.state = STATES.WIN; }
62: }
63: 
64: export { Game, STATES, FIXED_DT };

1: // js/main.js — W6: entry point (init, wire, start) — jogo completo
2: import C from './constants.js';
3: import { createEngine } from './engine.js';
4: import { buildLevel, cellAt } from './map.js';
5: import { Input } from './input.js';
6: import { PlayerEntity } from './player.js';
7: import { WeaponSystem } from './weapons.js';
8: import { spawnEnemies } from './enemies.js';
9: import { ParticleSystem } from './particles.js';
10: import { AudioEngine } from './audio.js';
11: import { buildMinimapData, renderMinimap } from './minimap.js';
12: import { buildHudData, renderHud } from './hud.js';
13: import { Game, STATES } from './game.js';
14: import { buildWorld, buildEnemyMeshes, buildViewmodel, createProjectileMesh } from './world.js';
15: import { raycastEnemy, meleeTarget } from './weapons.js';
16: import { knockback } from './move.js';
17: 
18: // WHY: monta o mundo do jogo (tudo que não depende do loop)
19: const init = () => {
20:   const canvas = document.getElementById('game');
21:   const engine = createEngine(canvas);
22:   engine.resize();
23:   const level = buildLevel();
24:   const input = new Input(canvas);
25:   const audio = new AudioEngine();
26:   const player = new PlayerEntity(level, input, new WeaponSystem());
27:   const enemies = spawnEnemies(level, 'imp', 6);
28:   const particles = new ParticleSystem();
29:   // WHY: buffers reais dos canvas overlay (hud = tela; minimap = 36×44 tiles × 6px)
30:   const hudCanvas = document.getElementById('hud');
31:   hudCanvas.width = window.innerWidth;
32:   hudCanvas.height = window.innerHeight;
33:   const mapCanvas = document.getElementById('minimap');
34:   mapCanvas.width = C.MAP.gridW * 6;
35:   mapCanvas.height = C.MAP.gridH * 6;
36:   const hudCtx = hudCanvas.getContext('2d');
37:   const mapCtx = mapCanvas.getContext('2d');
38:   return { engine, level, input, audio, player, enemies, particles, hudCtx, mapCtx, score: 0 };
39: };
40: 
41: // WHY: tela de menu/fim — texto central no canvas do HUD
42: const drawOverlay = (ctx, w, h, title, sub) => {
43:   // WHY: clearRect antes do fundo — evita ghosting do overlay anterior no canvas 2D
44:   ctx.clearRect(0, 0, w, h);
45:   ctx.fillStyle = 'rgba(0,0,0,0.72)';
46:   ctx.fillRect(0, 0, w, h);
47:   ctx.fillStyle = '#ffcc33';
48:   ctx.font = 'bold 28px monospace';
49:   ctx.textAlign = 'center';
50:   ctx.fillText(title, w / 2, h / 2 - 10);
51:   ctx.fillStyle = '#fff';
52:   ctx.font = '14px monospace';
53:   ctx.fillText(sub, w / 2, h / 2 + 20);
54: };
55: 
56: // WHY: liga update/render/estados ao loop fixed-step do Game
57: const wire = (w) => {
58:   buildWorld(w.engine.world, w.level.grid);
59:   const enemyMeshes = buildEnemyMeshes(w.engine.world, w.enemies);
60:   const viewmodel = buildViewmodel(w.engine.camera);
61:   const { camera, renderer, scene } = w.engine;
62:   let lastHp = w.player.hp;
63:   w.projectiles = [];
64: 
65:   // WHY: splash do foguete — dano a todos os inimigos na área (não ao player)
66:   const splashDamage = (x, z, radius, damage) => {
67:     for (const e of w.enemies) {
68:       if (e.dead) continue;
69:       const d = Math.hypot(e.pos.x - x, e.pos.z - z);
70:       if (d <= radius) e.damage(damage);
71:     }
72:   };
73: 
74:   // WHY: projétil do jogo com mesh visível — owner 'enemy' acerta player; 'player' acerta inimigos
75:   const pushProjectile = (from, dir, speed, damage, owner, splash = 0) => {
76:     w.projectiles.push({
77:       x: from.x, z: from.z,
78:       dir: { x: dir.x, z: dir.z },
79:       speed, damage, owner, splash,
80:       mesh: createProjectileMesh(scene, from.x, from.z),
81:     });
82:   };
83: 
84:   const update = (dt) => {
85:     if (w.game.state !== STATES.PLAYING) return;
86:     w.__updates = (w.__updates ?? 0) + 1; // WHY: contador p/ profiling fixed-step (E2E)
87:     w.player.update(dt);
88:     for (const e of w.enemies) {
89:       const evt = e.update(dt, w.player, w.level.grid);
90:       // WHY: melee/hitscan = dano direto; projectile/double/arc = projétil visível
91:       if (evt && evt.damage > 0) {
92:         if (evt.type === 'melee') {
93:           w.player.damage(evt.damage);
94:           knockback(w.player.vel, evt.from.x - w.player.pos.x, evt.from.z - w.player.pos.z, 2.5);
95:         } else if (evt.type === 'hitscan') {
96:           w.player.damage(evt.damage);
97:         } else if (evt.type === 'double') {
98:           const a = { x: evt.dir.x, z: evt.dir.z };
99:           const rot = (s) => ({ x: a.x * Math.cos(s) - a.z * Math.sin(s), z: a.x * Math.sin(s) + a.z * Math.cos(s) });
100:           pushProjectile(evt.from, rot(0.12), evt.speed ?? 6, evt.damage, 'enemy');
101:           pushProjectile(evt.from, rot(-0.12), evt.speed ?? 6, evt.damage, 'enemy');
102:         } else {
103:           pushProjectile(evt.from, evt.dir, evt.speed ?? 6, evt.damage, 'enemy');
104:         }
105:       }
106:       // WHY: score só na transição viva→morta — antes somava +10 todo frame (infinito)
107:       if (e.dead && !e.scored) { e.scored = true; w.score += 10; }
108:       const mesh = enemyMeshes.get(e);
109:       if (mesh) {
110:         if (e.dead) { if (mesh.parent) w.engine.world.remove(mesh); }
111:         else mesh.position.set(e.pos.x, e.stats.size * 0.8, e.pos.z);
112:       }
113:     }
114:     // WHY: projéteis — mover, colidir (parede/player/inimigo), dano + splash no impacto
115:     for (let i = w.projectiles.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
116:       const p = w.projectiles[i];
117:       p.x += p.dir.x * p.speed * dt;
118:       p.z += p.dir.z * p.speed * dt;
119:       const tile = cellAt(w.level.grid, Math.floor(p.x), Math.floor(p.z));
120:       if (tile === C.TILES.WALL || tile === C.TILES.DOOR) {
121:         if (p.splash > 0) splashDamage(p.x, p.z, p.splash, p.damage);
122:         w.engine.world.remove(p.mesh);
123:         w.projectiles.splice(i, 1);
124:         continue;
125:       }
126:       if (p.owner === 'enemy') {
127:         const dx = p.x - w.player.pos.x;
128:         const dz = p.z - w.player.pos.z;
129:         if (dx * dx + dz * dz < 0.36) {
130:           w.player.damage(p.damage);
131:           knockback(w.player.vel, p.dir.x, p.dir.z, 2.5);
132:           w.engine.world.remove(p.mesh);
133:           w.projectiles.splice(i, 1);
134:           continue;
135:         }
136:       } else {
137:         let hit = null;
138:         for (const e of w.enemies) {
139:           if (e.dead) continue;
140:           const dx = p.x - e.pos.x;
141:           const dz = p.z - e.pos.z;
142:           const r = e.stats.size * 0.6;
143:           if (dx * dx + dz * dz < r * r) { hit = e; break; }
144:         }
145:         if (hit) {
146:           hit.damage(p.damage);
147:           if (p.splash > 0) splashDamage(p.x, p.z, p.splash, p.damage);
148:           w.audio.play('explosion');
149:           w.engine.world.remove(p.mesh);
150:           w.projectiles.splice(i, 1);
151:           continue;
152:         }
153:       }
154:       p.mesh.position.set(p.x, 0.35, p.z);
155:     }
156:     w.particles.update(dt);
157:     if (w.player.hp < lastHp) w.audio.play('damage');
158:     lastHp = w.player.hp;
159:     // WHY: condições de fim — morte (lava/inimigos) ou saída (exit)
160:     if (w.player.hp <= 0) { w.game.gameOver(); w.audio.play('explosion'); return; }
161:     const tile = cellAt(w.level.grid, Math.floor(w.player.pos.x), Math.floor(w.player.pos.z));
162:     if (tile === C.TILES.EXIT) { w.game.win(); w.audio.play('pickup'); }
163:   };
164: 
165:   const render = () => {
166:     const hw = w.hudCtx.canvas.width;
167:     const hh = w.hudCtx.canvas.height;
168:     const st = w.game.state;
169:     if (st === STATES.MENU) { drawOverlay(w.hudCtx, hw, hh, 'DOOM CLONE', 'clique para jogar'); return; }
170:     if (st === STATES.GAMEOVER) { drawOverlay(w.hudCtx, hw, hh, 'VOCÊ MORREU', 'clique para tentar de novo'); return; }
171:     if (st === STATES.WIN) { drawOverlay(w.hudCtx, hw, hh, 'NÍVEL COMPLETO', `score ${w.score} — clique para jogar`); return; }
172:     if (st === STATES.PAUSED) { drawOverlay(w.hudCtx, hw, hh, 'PAUSA', 'P para continuar'); return; }
173:     // WHY: câmera FPS — posição + bob de caminhada + yaw/pitch do input
174:     camera.position.set(w.player.pos.x, w.player.viewY(), w.player.pos.z);
175:     camera.rotation.order = 'YXZ';
176:     camera.rotation.y = -w.player.yaw;
177:     camera.rotation.x = w.player.pitch;
178:     // WHY: viewmodel — 1 mesh visível por arma (filho da câmera)
179:     for (const [key, mesh] of viewmodel) mesh.visible = key === w.player.weapons.key;
180:     renderer.render(scene, camera);
181:     // WHY: HUD retro + minimap (overlays 2D)
182:     renderHud(w.hudCtx, buildHudData({ ...w.player, score: w.score }, w.player.weapons), hw, hh);
183:     renderMinimap(w.mapCtx, buildMinimapData(w.level, w.player, w.enemies, w.level.pickups), 6);
184:   };
185: 
186:   w.game = new Game({ update, render });
187:   w.audio.ensureCtx(); // autoplay policy: contexto criado no gesto do usuário
188:   document.getElementById('game').addEventListener('click', () => {
189:     if (w.game.state === STATES.MENU || w.game.state === STATES.GAMEOVER || w.game.state === STATES.WIN) {
190:       w.player.start();
191:       w.game.startGame();
192:     }
193:   });
194:   window.addEventListener('keydown', (e) => {
195:     if (e.code === 'KeyP') w.game.togglePause();
196:     // WHY: W8 — troca de arma (1-4) estava desconectada do browser
197:     const slot = ['Digit1', 'Digit2', 'Digit3', 'Digit4'].indexOf(e.code);
198:     if (slot !== -1 && w.game.state === STATES.PLAYING) w.player.weapons.switchWeapon(slot);
199:   });
200:   // WHY: W8 — tiro no mousedown; W9 — combate real: hitscan/spread/melee acertam
201:   // inimigos (raycastEnemy/meleeTarget); rocket vira projétil com dano no impacto
202:   document.addEventListener('mousedown', (e) => {
203:     if (e.button !== 0 || w.game.state !== STATES.PLAYING) return;
204:     const evt = w.player.weapons.fire(w.player, w.level.grid);
205:     if (!evt) return;
206:     if (evt.type === 'melee') {
207:       const t = meleeTarget(w.player, w.enemies, evt.range);
208:       if (t) { t.damage(evt.damage); w.audio.play('damage'); }
209:     } else if (evt.type === 'hitscan') {
210:       const t = raycastEnemy(w.player, w.level.grid, w.enemies, evt.hit.dist);
211:       if (t) { t.damage(evt.damage); w.audio.play('damage'); }
212:     } else if (evt.type === 'spread') {
213:       for (const pellet of evt.pellets) {
214:         const t = raycastEnemy(w.player, w.level.grid, w.enemies, pellet.dist);
215:         if (t) { t.damage(evt.damage); w.audio.play('damage'); }
216:       }
217:     } else if (evt.type === 'projectile') {
218:       const dir = { x: evt.proj.dx, z: evt.proj.dz };
219:       pushProjectile(w.player.pos, dir, evt.proj.speed, evt.damage, 'player', evt.splash ?? 0);
220:     }
221:   });
222: 
223:   w.game.start();
224:   // WHY: hook de teste E2E — Playwright lê/teleporta estado sem expor API pública
225:   window.__doom = w;
226:   return w;
227: };

231:   window.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', () => wire(init()));
232: }

16:   if (onGround) {
17:     vel.x *= 1 - C.PHYSICS.friction * dt;
18:     vel.z *= 1 - C.PHYSICS.friction * dt;
19:   } else {

23:   return vel;
24: };

26: // WHY: acelera o jogador na direção desejada
27: const accelerate = (vel, wishdir, accel, dt) => {
28:   vel.x += wishdir.x * accel * dt;
29:   vel.z += wishdir.z * accel * dt;
30:   return vel;
31: };

33: // WHY: move e resolve colisão AABB por eixo — checa a área varrida inteira
34: const moveAxis = (pos, vel, axis, dt, grid, radius) => {
35:   const newVel = { ...vel };
36:   const newPos = { ...pos };
37: 
38:   // WHY: eixo complementar (y é o eixo "outro" nos testes 2D)
39:   const other = axis === 'x' ? 'y' : 'x';
40:   const oldMain = pos[axis];
41:   const oldOther = pos[other];
42:   const newMain = oldMain + vel[axis] * dt;
43:   const newOther = oldOther + vel[other] * dt;
44: 
45:   // WHY: faixa varrida pelo AABB do centro antigo ao novo (+radius)
46:   const lo = Math.floor(Math.min(oldMain, newMain) - radius);
47:   const hi = Math.floor(Math.max(oldMain, newMain) + radius);
48:   const oLo = Math.floor(oldOther - radius);
49:   const oHi = Math.floor(newOther + radius);
50: 
51:   // WHY: fora do grid = parede (nunca `grid[r][c]` com r/c fora — isso lançaria
52:   // TypeError e mataria o rAF; o knockback do W9 empurra o player até a borda)
53:   const isWall = (r, c) => r < 0 || r >= grid.length || c < 0 || c >= grid[0].length || grid[r][c] === C.TILES.WALL;
54:   let collided = false;
55:   for (let a = lo; a <= hi && !collided; a++) {
56:     for (let b = oLo; b <= oHi; b++) {
57:       const cell = axis === 'x' ? isWall(b, a) : isWall(a, b);
58:       if (cell) { collided = true; break; }
59:     }
60:   }
61: 
62:   if (collided) {
63:     newVel[axis] = 0;
64:     newPos[axis] = oldMain;
65:   } else {
66:     newPos[axis] = newMain;

1: // js/game.js — W6: game loop fixed-step 60Hz + máquina de estados
2: // rAF injetável (browser real ou stub de teste); step() síncrono testável
3: 
4: const FIXED_DT = 1 / 60;
5: const MAX_FRAME = 0.25; // clamp contra tab switch (dt em segundos)
6: 
7: const STATES = { MENU: 'MENU', PLAYING: 'PLAYING', PAUSED: 'PAUSED', GAMEOVER: 'GAMEOVER', WIN: 'WIN' };
8: 
9: class Game {
10:   constructor({ update, render, requestFrame = null }) {
11:     this.update = update;
12:     this.render = render;
13:     // WHY: requestFrame injetável — browser usa rAF; testes usam stub/step direto
14:     this.requestFrame = requestFrame ?? ((cb) => {
15:       if (typeof window !== 'undefined' && window.requestAnimationFrame) window.requestAnimationFrame(cb);
16:     });
17:     this.state = STATES.MENU;
18:     this.time = 0;
19:     this.acc = 0;
20:     this.last = 0;
21:     this.frame = 0;
22:     this.running = false;
23:   }
24: 
25:   start() {
26:     if (this.running) return;
27:     this.running = true;
28:     this.last = performance.now();
29:     this.frame = 0;
30:     const loop = (now) => {
31:       if (!this.running) return;
32:       this.step(now);
33:       this.requestFrame(loop);
34:     };
35:     this.requestFrame(loop);
36:   }
37: 
38:   stop() { this.running = false; }
39: 
40:   // WHY: passo síncrono — acumula dt real e processa N passos fixos de 1/60
41:   step(now) {
42:     if (!this.running) return;
43:     const dt = Math.min(Math.max((now - this.last) / 1000, 0), MAX_FRAME);
44:     this.last = now;
45:     this.acc += dt;
46:     while (this.acc >= FIXED_DT) {
47:       // WHY: self-healing anti-freeze — exceção em update NUNCA mata o rAF
48:       // (bug W9: TypeError em moveAxis fora do grid congelava o jogo inteiro;
49:       // agora loga, descarta o passo e o loop continua vivo)
50:       try {
51:         this.update(FIXED_DT);
52:       } catch (err) {
53:         console.error('[game.step] update error:', err);
54:       }
55:       this.time += FIXED_DT;
56:       this.acc -= FIXED_DT;
57:       this.frame += 1;
58:     }
59:     try {
60:       this.render();
61:     } catch (err) {
62:       console.error('[game.step] render error:', err);
63:     }
64:   }
65: 
66:   // WHY: transições de estado (Menu→Play→Pause→GameOver/Win)
67:   startGame() { this.state = STATES.PLAYING; }
68:   pause() { if (this.state === STATES.PLAYING) this.state = STATES.PAUSED; }
69:   resume() { if (this.state === STATES.PAUSED) this.state = STATES.PLAYING; }
70:   togglePause() { if (this.state === STATES.PLAYING) this.pause(); else if (this.state === STATES.PAUSED) this.resume(); }
71:   gameOver() { this.state = STATES.GAMEOVER; }
72:   win() { this.state = STATES.WIN; }
73: }
74: 
75: export { Game, STATES, FIXED_DT };

5: import { R_y, clamp } from './utils.js';
6: 
7: // WHY: aplica gravidade ao vetor de velocidade (clamp só no limite inferior — não corta pulo)
8: const applyGravity = (vel, dt) => {
9:   vel.y += C.PHYSICS.gravity * dt;
10:   if (vel.y < C.PHYSICS.maxFall) vel.y = C.PHYSICS.maxFall;
11:   return vel;
12: };
13: 
14: // WHY: aplica atrito ou resistência do ar
15: const applyFriction = (vel, dt, onGround) => {
16:   if (onGround) {
17:     vel.x *= 1 - C.PHYSICS.friction * dt;
18:     vel.z *= 1 - C.PHYSICS.friction * dt;
19:   } else {
20:     vel.x *= 1 - C.PHYSICS.airResist * dt;
21:     vel.z *= 1 - C.PHYSICS.airResist * dt;
22:   }
23:   return vel;
24: };
25: 
26: // WHY: acelera o jogador na direção desejada
27: const accelerate = (vel, wishdir, accel, dt) => {
28:   vel.x += wishdir.x * accel * dt;
29:   vel.z += wishdir.z * accel * dt;
30:   return vel;
31: };
32: 
33: // WHY: move e resolve colisão AABB por eixo — checa a área varrida inteira
34: const moveAxis = (pos, vel, axis, dt, grid, radius) => {
35:   const newVel = { ...vel };
36:   const newPos = { ...pos };
37: 
38:   // WHY: eixo complementar (y é o eixo "outro" nos testes 2D)
39:   const other = axis === 'x' ? 'y' : 'x';
40:   const oldMain = pos[axis];
41:   const oldOther = pos[other];
42:   const newMain = oldMain + vel[axis] * dt;
43:   const newOther = oldOther + vel[other] * dt;
44: 
45:   // WHY: faixa varrida pelo AABB do centro antigo ao novo (+radius)
46:   const lo = Math.floor(Math.min(oldMain, newMain) - radius);
47:   const hi = Math.floor(Math.max(oldMain, newMain) + radius);
48:   const oLo = Math.floor(oldOther - radius);
49:   const oHi = Math.floor(newOther + radius);
50: 
51:   // WHY: fora do grid = parede (nunca `grid[r][c]` com r/c fora — isso lançaria
52:   // TypeError e mataria o rAF; o knockback do W9 empurra o player até a borda)
53:   const isWall = (r, c) => r < 0 || r >= grid.length || c < 0 || c >= grid[0].length || grid[r][c] === C.TILES.WALL;
54:   let collided = false;
55:   for (let a = lo; a <= hi && !collided; a++) {
56:     for (let b = oLo; b <= oHi; b++) {
57:       const cell = axis === 'x' ? isWall(b, a) : isWall(a, b);
58:       if (cell) { collided = true; break; }
59:     }
60:   }
61: 
62:   if (collided) {
63:     newVel[axis] = 0;
64:     newPos[axis] = oldMain;
65:   } else {
66:     newPos[axis] = newMain;
67:     newPos[other] = newOther;
68:   }
69: 
70:   return { pos: newPos, vel: newVel, collided };
71: };
72: 
73: // WHY: aplica pulo quando no chão
74: const tryJump = (vel, onGround) => {
75:   if (onGround) vel.y = C.PHYSICS.jumpVel;
76:   return vel;
77: };
78: 
79: // WHY: aplica knockback ao jogador
80: const knockback = (vel, dirX, dirZ, force) => {
81:   vel.x += dirX * force * C.PHYSICS.BOUNCE;
82:   vel.z += dirZ * force * C.PHYSICS.BOUNCE;
83:   return vel;
84: };
85: 
86: // WHY: calcula dano de splash por distância
87: const splashDamage = (damage, dist, radius) => {
88:   if (dist > radius) return 0;
89:   if (dist === 0) return damage;
90:   return damage * (1 - dist / radius);
91: };
92: 
93: // WHY: bobbing da câmera
94: const cameraBob = (time, moving, speed) => {
95:   const bobAmp = C.PHYSICS.bobAmp;
96:   const bobFreq = C.PHYSICS.bobFreq;
97:   if (!moving) return { x: 0, y: 0 };
98:   return {
99:     x: Math.sin(time * bobFreq) * bobAmp,
100:     y: Math.sin(time * bobFreq * 2) * bobAmp * 0.5,
101:   };
102: };
103: 
104: export {
105:   applyGravity,
106:   applyFriction,
107:   accelerate,
108:   moveAxis,
109:   tryJump,
110:   knockback,
111:   splashDamage,
112:   cameraBob,
113: };

1: // js/player.js — PlayerEntity (W3): FSM MENU/PLAYING, física, bob, pickups
2: import C from './constants.js';
3: import {
4:   applyGravity,
5:   applyFriction,
6:   accelerate,
7:   moveAxis,
8:   tryJump,
9:   cameraBob,
10: } from './move.js';
11: 
12: const { floor, min, max } = Math;
13: 
14: class PlayerEntity {
15:   constructor(level, input, weapons) {
16:     const s = level.playerSpawn;
17:     // WHY: centro do tile (spawn.x/z são índices inteiros do grid)
18:     this.pos = { x: s.x + 0.5, z: s.z + 0.5 };
19:     this.y = 0;
20:     this.vel = { x: 0, z: 0, y: 0 };
21:     this.yaw = s.yaw ?? -Math.PI / 2;
22:     this.pitch = 0;
23:     this.hp = C.PLAYER.startHp;
24:     this.armor = C.PLAYER.startArmor;
25:     this.onGround = true;
26:     this.state = 'MENU'; // FSM: MENU -> PLAYING
27:     this.bobTime = 0;
28:     this.input = input;
29:     this.weapons = weapons;
30:     this.level = level;
31:   }
32: 
33:   // WHY: FSM — transições explícitas (lição 5: compare uppercase, comente cada transição)
34:   start() { this.state = 'PLAYING'; }
35:   pause() { this.state = 'MENU'; }
36: 
37:   isMoving() {
38:     return Math.abs(this.vel.x) > 0.05 || Math.abs(this.vel.z) > 0.05;
39:   }
40: 
41:   update(dt) {
42:     if (this.state !== 'PLAYING') return;
43:     // WHY: cooldown das armas avança com o tempo de jogo (W8 — sem isso o browser
44:     // nunca decrementava o cooldown e canFire() ficava false após o 1º tiro)
45:     this.weapons.update(dt);
46:     const wish = this.input.getAxis();
47:     const yaw = this.input.yaw;
48: 
49:     // WHY: R_y(-yaw) — câmera usa rotation.y = -yaw, então frente = (sin yaw, -cos yaw);
50:     // R_y(+yaw) deixava W/S invertidos em relação à câmera (bug "teclas WS invertidas")
51:     const wishX = -wish.z * Math.sin(yaw) + wish.x * Math.cos(yaw);
52:     const wishZ = wish.z * Math.cos(yaw) + wish.x * Math.sin(yaw);
53: 
54:     const speed = this.input.isDown('ShiftLeft') ? C.PHYSICS.runSpeed : C.PHYSICS.walkSpeed;
55:     accelerate(this.vel, { x: wishX, z: wishZ }, C.PHYSICS.accel * speed, dt);
56:     applyFriction(this.vel, dt, this.onGround);
57:     if (this.input.isDown('Space')) tryJump(this.vel, this.onGround);
58:     applyGravity(this.vel, dt);
59: 
60:     // WHY: colisão horizontal por eixo — moveAxis usa pos {x,y} do grid 2D,
61:     // então traduzimos para {x: col, y: row} e de volta para pos {x,z}
62:     const gp = { x: this.pos.x, y: this.pos.z };
63:     const rX = moveAxis(gp, { x: this.vel.x, y: this.vel.z }, 'x', dt, this.level.grid, C.PLAYER.radius);
64:     const rZ = moveAxis(rX.pos, { x: rX.vel.x, y: rX.vel.y }, 'y', dt, this.level.grid, C.PLAYER.radius);
65:     this.pos.x = rZ.pos.x;
66:     this.pos.z = rZ.pos.y;
67:     this.vel.x = rZ.vel.x;
68:     this.vel.z = rZ.vel.y;
69: 
70:     // WHY: altura vertical — chão em y=0, sem teto no mapa
71:     this.y += this.vel.y * dt;
72:     if (this.y <= 0) {
73:       this.y = 0;
74:       this.vel.y = 0;
75:       this.onGround = true;
76:     } else if (this.vel.y !== 0) {
77:       this.onGround = false;
78:     }
79: 
80:     if (this.isMoving()) this.bobTime += dt;
81:     this.yaw = yaw;
82:     this.pitch = this.input.pitch;
83: 
84:     this.stepHazards(dt);
85:     this.collectPickups();
86:   }
87: 
88:   // WHY: lava causa dano contínuo (tile LAVA do grid)
89:   // WHY: guard de bounds — se o player sair do grid (knockback extremo), grid[z] é
90:   // undefined e `undefined[x]` lançaria TypeError, matando o rAF (jogo congela)
91:   stepHazards(dt) {
92:     const row = this.level.grid[floor(this.pos.z)];
93:     const tile = row ? row[floor(this.pos.x)] : undefined;
94:     if (tile === C.TILES.LAVA) this.damage(12 * dt);
95:   }
96: 
97:   collectPickups() {
98:     const remaining = [];
99:     for (const p of this.level.pickups) {
100:       const d = Math.hypot(p.x + 0.5 - this.pos.x, p.z + 0.5 - this.pos.z);
101:       if (d < 0.6) {
102:         if (p.type === C.TILES.HEALTH) this.hp = min(C.PLAYER.startHp, this.hp + 25);
103:         else if (p.type === C.TILES.ARMOR) this.armor = min(100, this.armor + 25);
104:         // WHY: W9 — pickup W desbloqueia arma nova (shotgun → rocket) e SEMPRE dá
105:         // munição; antes só dava munição e o inventário já vinha completo (DOOM clássico)
106:         else if (p.type === C.TILES.WEAPON) {
107:           if (!this.weapons.inventory.includes('shotgun')) this.weapons.unlockWeapon('shotgun');
108:           else if (!this.weapons.inventory.includes('rocket')) this.weapons.unlockWeapon('rocket');
109:           this.weapons.addAmmo('all', 20);
110:         }
111:       } else {
112:         remaining.push(p);
113:       }
114:     }
115:     this.level.pickups = remaining;
116:   }
117: 
118:   // WHY: armadura absorve 50% do dano antes do HP (DOOM clássico)
119:   // WHY: sem Math.round — dano contínuo (lava 12*dt com dt<1/12) seria anulado
120:   damage(amount) {
121:     if (this.armor > 0) {
122:       const absorbed = min(this.armor, amount * 0.5);
123:       this.armor -= absorbed;
124:       amount -= absorbed;
125:     }
126:     this.hp = max(0, this.hp - amount);
127:     return this.hp;
128:   }
129: 
130:   viewY() {
131:     return C.PLAYER.height + cameraBob(this.bobTime, this.isMoving(), 1).y;
132:   }
133: }
134: 
135: export { PlayerEntity };
